title: Zorn's Self Confidence
content: Anders Zorn (1860-1920) painted this portrait of an executioner in Siebenbürgen (Transylvania) while he was on his honeymoon in 1885.Just 25 years old, Zorn was brimming with self confidence. "I never spent much time thinking about others' art. I felt that if I wanted to become something, then I had to go after nature with all my interest and energy, seek what I loved about it, and desire to steal its secret and beauty. I was entitled to become as great as anyone else, and in that branch of art so commanded by me, watercolor painting, I considered myself to have already surpassed all predecessors and contemporaries."He later translated the portrait into an etching, which is necessarily reversed.The quote comes from Zorn's autobiographical notes, included in the recent bookAnders Zorn: Sweden's Master Painter(Book review on this blog)On the web:Anders Zorn: The Complete Works
